podcast.title: Joining Red Hot Chili Peppers (December 1988)
podcast.body: Chad Smith auditioned for the Red Hot Chili Peppers and secured the drummer position in December 1988, just weeks after John Frusciante joined as guitarist. This completed the lineup that would become known as the classic Red Hot Chili Peppers, debuting on "Mother's Milk" by early 1989. "And that's when Chad Smith auditioned and got the job in December just a few weeks after John signed up."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Refusal to Stay at The Mansion (1991)
podcast.body: During the recording of "Blood Sugar Sex Magik" at the historic mansion at 351 Laurel Canyon, Chad Smith was "allegedly too freaked out by the vibes of the place" and refused to stay there during the recording sessions, unlike the other three band members. "Chad Smith was allegedly too freaked out by the vibes of the place so he refused to stay there during sessions."

podcast.title: Biggest Drum Set Performance (2006)
podcast.body: Chad Smith holds the Guinness Book of World Records title for performing with the biggest drum set, a monstrous 308-piece kit. This one-off performance in 2006 was for Pearl Drums, a manufacturer he endorses, and was done as a favor to a friend who owned a music store, rather than for touring. "Chad played a stupidly-large drum kit that consisted of 300 and 8 pieces."

podcast.title: Catalyst for John Frusciante's Reunion
podcast.body: Chad Smith played a pivotal role in initiating the discussion for John Frusciante's return to the Red Hot Chili Peppers. At Flea's wedding, Chad told John that he missed playing with him and suggested that he, John, and Flea should jam sometime. "Chad had said something to me when I saw him at Flea's wedding. And he was like, he misses playing with me and him and Flea should jam sometime."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Early Formation of the Classic Lineup (1988-1989)
xref.body: Following the death of Hillel Slovak and the departure of Jack Irons in June 1988, the band auditioned Dwayne "Blackbird" McKnight, but he didn't work out. John Frusciante joined as guitarist in October 1988, followed by Chad Smith as drummer in December 1988. By early 1989, this new lineup of Frusciante, Smith, Flea, and Anthony Kiedis formed what would become known as the classic Red Hot Chili Peppers configuration, debuting on the album "Mother's Milk." "By the start of 1989, the Chili Peppers had undergone a complete refurbishment. John was the new guitarist and Chad was the new drummer."

xref.title: "Blood Sugar Sex Magik" Recording Location (April 1991)
xref.body: For the recording of "Blood Sugar Sex Magik," the Red Hot Chili Peppers moved into a historic mansion at 351 Laurel Canyon Boulevard, built in 1918. The house, with a reputation for being haunted and allegedly having secret tunnels to the nearby "Houdini Estate," was chosen by producer Rick Rubin for its isolated vibe. A Canadian company converted the basement into a recording studio. Chad Smith, however, was too unnerved by the house's atmosphere to stay there during sessions. "In April 1991, the Chili Peppers moved into a historic mansion at 351 Laurel Canyon, Boulevard that was built in 1918."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Long Strange Trip of John Frusciante Part 1

xref.title: Inspiration from The Mansion – Blood Sugar Sex Magik Recording (1991)
xref.body: During the recording of "Blood Sugar Sex Magik" in a historic mansion, John Frusciante embraced the isolated and reputedly haunted environment. Unlike Chad Smith, who refused to stay there, Frusciante loved the house and found it inspirational, ready to disconnect from the outside world. He believed friendly ghosts resided there and even mused that the spirit of a person who died in the house might have influenced his guitar sound. "There are definitely ghosts in this house, said John, but they are very friendly."

xref.title: One-Off Drummers Group for Live Earth (2007)
xref.body: SOS All Stars was a unique, one-off group comprised of drummers Taylor Hawkins, Roger Taylor (Queen), and Chad Smith (Red Hot Chili Peppers), assembled specifically for the Live Earth show in London in 2007. This project highlighted a special gathering of influential rock drummers. "This was a one-off drummers group, but together for the live earth show in London in 2007."

xref.title: SOS All Stars (2007) - One-Off Drummer Supergroup
xref.body: Taylor Hawkins participated in SOS All Stars, a special one-off drummers' group formed for the Live Earth show in London in 2007. He was joined by Roger Taylor of Queen and Chad Smith of the Red Hot Chili Peppers, showcasing his connections within the drumming community. xref.title: Chad Smith's Audition and Background
xref.body: Chad Smith, a hard-hitting drummer from Detroit, was influenced by the relaxed rhythms of Motown. He was the last of 30 people to audition for the drummer position in 1989. Despite almost not making it through, a connection "clicked" in Flea's mind when they jammed, and Smith has been a member ever since. "He was the last guy in a line of 30 people to audition for the gig when it became available in 1989."

xref.title: Chad Smith's Reunion Catalyst
xref.body: The idea for John Frusciante's return was sparked by Chad Smith, who told John at Flea's wedding that he missed playing with him and suggested they, along with Flea, should jam sometime. This casual comment initiated the chain of events leading to John's rejoining the band. "Chad had said something to me when I saw him at Flea's wedding. And he was like, he misses playing with me and him and Flea should jam sometime."

xref.title: Exceptional Rhythm Section
xref.body: The band is known for having one of the great rhythm sections in New Rock, formed by Flea on bass and Chad Smith on drums. This "funky rhythm section that rocks" provides a strong foundation for the band's sound. "The Red Hot Chili Peppers featuring the backbone of Flea on bass and Chad Smith on drums and together they form one of the great rhythm sections in all of New Rock."

xref.title: Firing Due to Addiction and Replacement
xref.body: Unfortunately, D.H. Peligro's struggles with drug and alcohol demons led to his firing later in 1988, which then paved the way for Chad Smith to join the group as drummer. "Unfortunately Pellegros had his own drug and alcohol demons and was fired later the same year, paving the way for Chad Smith to join the group."

xref.title: Flea's Direct Rejoining Offer
xref.body: After John Frusciante mentioned Chad Smith's suggestion about jamming, Flea, within seconds, directly asked John if he would consider being in the Red Hot Chili Peppers again. This swift proposition quickly moved the conversation from a casual jam to a potential full-time reunion. "It was within seconds after I suggested that Flea was like, you ever think about being in the Red Hat Chili Peppers again?"

xref.title: High Guitarist Turnover Rate
xref.body: The band has a notable history of high turnover for its guitarists, with the observation that "Being a guitarist in the Chili Peppers is the equivalent of being an extra in a red shirt on Star Trek." Drummer Chad Smith and the core duo of Flea and Anthony Kiedis are seen as exceptions to this pattern. "If you're in the Red Hot Chili Peppers and your name isn't Flea or Anthry, you are on Boroughed Time."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: You're Fired!

xref.title: Initiator of Reunion Talks
xref.body: The conversation about John Frusciante rejoining the band was initiated by him after Chad Smith expressed missing playing with him at Flea's wedding. John then suggested jamming to Flea, which quickly led to Flea asking him to rejoin. "Chad had said something to me when I saw him at Flea's wedding. And he was like, he misses playing with me and him and Flea should jam sometime. So I mentioned it to Flea."

xref.title: St. Paul Origins and Early Influences
xref.body: Chad Smith, a hard-hitting and rock-solid drummer, started playing drums at the age of seven in St. Paul, Minnesota. Initially, he was a straight-ahead rock drummer, taking inspiration from bands like Black Sabbath, The Rolling Stones, The Beatles, The Who, and Led Zeppelin. "He's from St. Paul, Minnesota, started playing when he was seven."

xref.title: Transition to Musician with Larry Frentangelo
xref.body: Chad Smith's approach to drumming fundamentally changed after he received instruction from a funk drummer named Larry Frentangelo. Following this experience, Chad stated that he evolved from merely being a drummer to becoming a musician, indicating a deeper understanding and application of his craft. "But then he was given instruction by a funk drummer named Larry Frentangelo."
